questions.q: If the x-coordinate of a point is zero, the point lies —
questions.work: x = distance from the y-axis. x = 0 means the point is on the y-axis, e.g. (0, 5).

questions.q: If the y-coordinate of a point is zero, the point lies —
questions.work: y = 0 means the point is at zero height — on the x-axis, e.g. (3, 0).

questions.q: A point both of whose coordinates are negative lies in —
questions.work: Signs: I (+, +), II (−, +), III (−, −), IV (+, −). Both negative ⇒ quadrant III.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, match the columns or true/false).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) If the distance between A(0, 0) and B(x, 3) is 5 units, x = ____. (ii) If the midpoint of (x, 4) and (5, 12) is (4, 8), x = ____.
Fill in the blanks: (i) The distance of P(−2, 3) from the y-axis is ____. (ii) The distance between (5 cos 35°, 0) and (0, 5 cos 55°) is ____.
Match: (i) If P(−1, 1) is the midpoint of A(−3, b) and B(1, b + 4), b = ____ (ii) The perimeter of the triangle with vertices (0, 4), (0, 0), (3, 0) is ____ — (A) −1 (B) 12 (C) 1 (D) 7

Write True or False (any two): (i) (0, −4) lies in quadrant IV. (ii) The distance of (2, −3) from the x-axis is 3. (iii) The midpoint of (1, 0) and (3, −2) is (−2, −1). (iv) A circle with centre O through (2, −3) has radius √13.
questions.answer:
(i) False: x = 0, so it lies on the y-axis.
(ii) True: |y| = 3.
(iii) False: ((1 + 3)/2, (0 − 2)/2) = (2, −1).
(iv) True: √(2² + 3²) = √13.

questions.q: Write True or False: (i) R(−2, −3) lies in quadrant III. (ii) The point (0, 5) lies on the x-axis.
questions.answer:
(i) True: both coordinates are negative.
(ii) False: x = 0, so it lies on the y-axis.

questions.q: Find a point on the x-axis which is equidistant from (7, 6) and (−3, 4).
questions.answer:
Let it be P(x, 0). PA² = PB²: (x − 7)² + 36 = (x + 3)² + 16.
x² − 14x + 85 = x² + 6x + 25 ⇒ 20x = 60 ⇒ x = 3.
The point is (3, 0).

questions.q: A circle has centre (2, 0) and passes through (7, −12). Find its diameter.
If P(4, −2) is the midpoint of A(5k, 2) and B(−k, −6), find k.
A line MN cuts the x-axis at M(6, 0) and the y-axis at N(0, 8). Find MN.
Find the ratio in which the y-axis divides the join of (4, −5) and (−1, 2). Also find the point of division.
questions.answer:
Let the ratio be k : 1. x-coordinate of the point = (k(−1) + 1 × 4)/(k + 1) = 0 (on the y-axis) ⇒ −k + 4 = 0 ⇒ k = 4.
Ratio 4 : 1.
y = (4 × 2 + 1 × (−5))/5 = 3/5. The point is (0, 3/5).

or.q: Show that A(1, 5), B(7, −1) and C(4, 2) are collinear.
or.answer:
AC = √[(4 − 1)² + (2 − 5)²] = √18 = 3√2.
CB = √[(7 − 4)² + (−1 − 2)²] = √18 = 3√2.
AB = √[(7 − 1)² + (−1 − 5)²] = √72 = 6√2.
AC + CB = 6√2 = AB, so the points are collinear (C lies between A and B — in fact it is the midpoint).

questions.q: Find the value of m if the points (3, 1), (−2, −3) and (8, 2m) are collinear.
Prove that O(0, 0), A(4, 3) and B(8, 6) are collinear.
questions.answer:
OA = √(16 + 9) = 5; AB = √(16 + 9) = 5; OB = √(64 + 36) = 10.
OA + AB = 10 = OB, so the three points are collinear.

questions.q: The vertices of △ABC are A(4, −3), B(11, 5) and C(6, 1). Find the lengths of its sides and its centroid.
Find the area of the triangle with vertices A(3, 0), B(7, 0) and C(8, 4).
questions.answer:
A and B lie on the x-axis, so base AB = 4 and height = y-coordinate of C = 4.
Area = ½ × 4 × 4 = 8 sq units.
(Formula: ½|3(0 − 4) + 7(4 − 0) + 8(0 − 0)| = ½|−12 + 28| = 8.)

questions.q: Find the area of the quadrilateral ABCD with vertices A(1, 2), B(6, 2), C(5, 3) and D(3, 4).
Find the area of the rhombus with vertices A(3, 0), B(4, 5), C(−1, 4) and D(−2, −1). Also find the distance between its sides AB and CD.
questions.answer:
Diagonals: AC = √[(−1 − 3)² + (4 − 0)²] = √32 = 4√2; BD = √[(−2 − 4)² + (−1 − 5)²] = √72 = 6√2.
Area = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = ½ × 4√2 × 6√2 = 24 sq units.
Side AB = √(1 + 25) = √26. A rhombus is a parallelogram, so area = base × height:
24 = √26 × h ⇒ h = 24/√26 ≈ 4.71 units — the distance between AB and CD.

questions.q: The vertices of a triangle are A(2, 1), B(6, 4) and C(2, 4). (i) Find the lengths of the sides. (ii) Show it is right-angled. (iii) Find its centroid and area.
